bench-bot: [bench-run 2026-03-10T14:02:00Z] finished sweep: model=open-llama-7b | variants=fp16,q4f16,q5_k_m | gpus=H100,A100 | regions=us-east1,europe-west1,asia-southeast1 | seq=512/1024/2048
bench-bot: quick summary (p50_prefill / p95_decode / tok/s / $/1M toks):
  us-east1 H100 q4f16: 28ms / 112ms / 14.2k tok/s / $7.6
  us-east1 A100 q4f16: 33ms / 135ms / 11.8k tok/s / $6.1
  europe-west1 H100 q4f16: 30ms / 128ms / 13.0k tok/s / $8.2
  asia-southeast1 H100 q4f16: 42ms / 210ms / 9.1k tok/s / $14.9
  NOTE: q5_k_m had ~10-12% decode perf regression on H100 for seq>=2048 due to kernel fallback.

maria.lopez: wow asia numbers are wild. is that all compute, or network/egress getting counted? :thinking:

raj.kapoor: compute-only for these. asia higher $/1M is mostly lower throughput (tok/s) on stock images + observed kernel fallback on H100 there. no egress.

tyler.ng: confirmed the fallback — H100 vendor kernel selector picks the optimized fused-attn for seq<=1024, then falls back to generic attention for long sequences on the otherwise-updated driver in asia-southeast1. p95 spikes immediately.

jen.sullivan: can you paste the detection rule? we need to know if this will affect Dedicated capacity sizing for APAC customers.

raj.kapoor: detection snippet i used:
```
# kernel_fallback_detector (very small)
if metrics.attn_kernel == "generic" and seq_len >= 2048:
  flag = "fallback_attn_long_seq"
```

bench-bot: repro command (used for the sweep):
```
run_bench --model open-llama-7b --variant q4f16 --gpu H100 --region asia-southeast1 --batch 1 --seq 2048 --warm 100 --it 500 --trace kernels
```

maria.lopez: so does A100 avoid the fallback at seq>=2048?

tyler.ng: A100 still uses a different kernel path that stays optimized for this model/quant on the tested driver stack. result: A100 p95_decode ~= 135ms vs H100 210ms in asia for same config. that's why $/1M ends up lower on A100 despite worse p50.

jen.sullivan: high-level ask from product: for customers targeting 99th percentile latency SLAs in APAC, do we advise A100 reserved SKU or H100 with pinned kernel build? what's the short recommendation?

raj.kapoor: short: for long-seq workloads (>1024) in APAC, either:
  - use A100 reserved (more predictable $/1M now), or
  - use H100 but pin a custom runtime/kernel that includes fused long-attn (we have a build that removes fallback) — ops must deploy that image in Private/Dedicated.

tyler.ng: also quant profile matters: q5_k_m reduces tokens/sec slightly but improves model quality. if customer prioritizes perf/cost, q4f16 on A100 is the sweet spot for APAC right now.

maria.lopez: any charts to attach for the customer deck? small ascii table would help.

bench-bot: pasted mini table (seq=2048, batch=1):
  GPU | variant | p95_decode(ms) | tok/s | $/1M
  ----+---------+----------------+-------+------
  H100 | q4f16 | 210 | 9.1k | $14.9
  A100 | q4f16 | 135 | 11.8k | $6.1
  H100*| q4f16+patched | 140 | 12.5k | $8.1
  *patched = fused-attn kernel pinned

jen.sullivan: perfect. can we get a followup task to run the same sweep but with KV-cache-heavy chat workloads (prefill larger, decode shorter, mixed seq)? i want to show impact on end-to-end latency for chat apps.

tyler.ng: ack, i'll schedule a focused chat-sweep next week and include driver's kernel build matrix + quant profiles. tagging @raj for infra image work.

raj.kapoor: noted. will prepare a Dedicated image with the fused-attn kernel for APAC region tests and drop the image tag in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:

maria.lopez: thanks all — this explains the "weird" cost numbers. will synthesize a 1-slide summary for sales + AMs.
